# @forgesworn/ring-sig — Full API Reference

> SAG and LSAG ring signatures on secp256k1. Prove group membership without revealing identity, with optional double-action detection via linkable key images.

Package: `@forgesworn/ring-sig`
Repository: https://github.com/forgesworn/ring-sig
Nostr: npub1mgvlrnf5hm9yf0n5mf9nqmvarhvxkc6remu5ec3vf8r0txqkuk7su0e7q2
Licence: MIT

## Install

```bash
npm install @forgesworn/ring-sig
```

## What This Library Does

A ring signature proves "one of these N public keys signed this message" without revealing which one. The verifier learns nothing about the signer's identity — only that they are a member of the specified ring.

Two variants are provided:

- **SAG** (Spontaneous Anonymous Group) — pure anonymity. No linkability at all. Good for one-off attestations, whistleblowing, and group membership proofs.
- **LSAG** (Linkable SAG) — anonymity plus double-action detection. Signatures from the same key in the same context share a deterministic key image, enabling voting, rate-limiting, and double-spend prevention without deanonymisation.

## Key Format Conventions

All public keys are **x-only hex**: 32 bytes, 64 hex characters, following the BIP-340 convention used by Nostr and Bitcoin Taproot. Public key hex is case-insensitive; the library normalises it to lowercase (signatures carry the lowercase ring). Internally the library prepends `02` (even y-coordinate) to convert to a compressed point.

Private keys are standard 32-byte scalars as hex, and must be **exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, below the curve order N**. Uppercase, short or oversized hex, and values at or above N, throw `ValidationError` (they are rejected, not reduced). The same rule applies to the `c0` and `responses` scalars of a signature; signatures produced by this library always satisfy it.

The library applies a BIP-340 parity fix: if `x*G` has odd y, `x` is negated before use, ensuring the derived public key always matches the stored x-only form.

### Generating keys

`@noble/curves` and `@noble/hashes` are dependencies of this package; add them to your own `package.json` if you import them directly. Import paths need the `.js` suffix, and `getPublicKey` takes bytes, not a hex string. `schnorr.getPublicKey` returns the x-only public key directly:

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey), // 64 lowercase hex characters
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only, 64 hex characters
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.publicKey);
```

### Input limits

| Input | Limit |
|-------|-------|
| `ring` | 2 to 1000 members, no duplicates (`MAX_RING_SIZE`) |
| `message` | string, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes |
| `electionId` | non-empty string, at most 512 UTF-8 bytes (enforced by `lsagSign` and `lsagVerify`) |

## Entry Point

ESM-only. Single entry point:

```typescript
import {
  ringSign,
  ringVerify,
  lsagSign,
  lsagVerify,
  computeKeyImage,
  hasDuplicateKeyImage,
  RingSignatureError,
  ValidationError,
  CryptoError,
  MAX_RING_SIZE,
} from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';
```

`MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` and `MAX_ELECTION_ID_BYTES` exist in the source modules but are not exported from the entry point.

---

## SAG — Spontaneous Anonymous Group Signatures

### Type: `RingSignature`

```typescript
interface RingSignature {
  /** The ring of public keys (x-only hex, 32 bytes each) */
  ring: string[];
  /** Starting challenge scalar c_0 (hex) */
  c0: string;
  /** Response scalars s_0 … s_{n-1} (hex) — one per ring member */
  responses: string[];
  /** The signed message (plaintext, stored verbatim) */
  message: string;
  /** Domain separator — omitted when using the default 'sag-v1' */
  domain?: string;
}
```

### `ringSign`

```typescript
function ringSign(
  message: string,
  ring: string[],
  signerIndex: number,
  privateKey: string,
  domain?: string,   // default: 'sag-v1'
): RingSignature
```

Produces a SAG ring signature. The signer proves membership in `ring` without revealing their position.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `message` | `string` | Message to sign. Hashed internally. Any UTF-8 string, at most 65536 bytes. |
| `ring` | `string[]` | Array of x-only public key hex strings (32 bytes each). Minimum 2, maximum 1000. Must have no duplicates. |
| `signerIndex` | `number` | Integer index of the actual signer in `ring`. Must satisfy `0 <= signerIndex < ring.length`. |
| `privateKey` | `string` | Signer's private key: 64 lowercase hex characters below the curve order. Must correspond to `ring[signerIndex]`. |
| `domain` | `string` | Optional 5th argument: domain separator for cross-protocol isolation. Defaults to `'sag-v1'`. Verifiers read it from the signature; see Domain Separators. |

**Returns** a `RingSignature` object. The signature is serialisable to JSON.

**Throws**
- `ValidationError`: ring too small/large, duplicate members, index out of range or not an integer, private key not 64 lowercase hex or not below the curve order, key mismatch, message over 65536 bytes.
- A ring entry that is not a valid x-only curve point surfaces the underlying `@noble/curves` error, and a non-string ring entry a `TypeError`.

**Example**

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { ringSign } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.publicKey);

// Sign as ring member at index 1 — identity hidden from verifier
const sig = ringSign('Hello, world!', ring, 1, keyPairs[1].privateKey);

// Serialisable — safe to send over the wire
console.log(JSON.stringify(sig));
```

---

### `ringVerify`

```typescript
function ringVerify(sig: RingSignature): boolean
```

Verifies a SAG ring signature. Returns `true` if valid, `false` otherwise. Never throws: all errors (including a `null` or otherwise malformed `sig`) are caught and returned as `false`.

The domain is taken from `sig.domain`, or `'sag-v1'` when that field is absent. There is no expected-domain parameter. Verification only proves the signature is consistent with the ring, message and domain it carries; it does not know which ring, message or domain you expect. See Domain Separators and the Verifier Checklist.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `sig` | `RingSignature` | The ring signature to verify. |

**Returns** `boolean` — `true` if the signature is valid, `false` for any malformed input or verification failure.

**Example**

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { ringSign, ringVerify } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.publicKey);
const sig = ringSign('Hello, world!', ring, 1, keyPairs[1].privateKey);

const valid = ringVerify(sig);
console.log(valid); // true

// Tamper with the message — verification fails
const tampered = { ...sig, message: 'Different message' };
console.log(ringVerify(tampered)); // false
```

---

## LSAG — Linkable Spontaneous Anonymous Group Signatures

### Type: `LsagSignature`

```typescript
interface LsagSignature {
  /** Key image I = x * H_p(P || electionId) — compressed point hex (66 hex chars / 33 bytes) */
  keyImage: string;
  /** Starting challenge scalar c_0 (hex) */
  c0: string;
  /** Response scalars s_0 … s_{n-1} (hex) — one per ring member */
  responses: string[];
  /** The ring of public keys (x-only hex, 32 bytes each) */
  ring: string[];
  /** The signed message (plaintext, stored verbatim) */
  message: string;
  /** Binds the key image to this specific election/context */
  electionId: string;
  /** Domain separator — omitted when using the default 'lsag-v1' */
  domain?: string;
}
```

The `keyImage` field is a **compressed secp256k1 point** — 33 bytes, `02` or `03` prefix, 66 hex characters total. It is deterministically derived from the signer's private key and the `electionId`. Two LSAG signatures share a key image if and only if they were produced by the same private key for the same `electionId`.

---

### `lsagSign`

```typescript
function lsagSign(
  message: string,
  ring: string[],
  signerIndex: number,
  privateKey: string,
  electionId: string,
  domain?: string,   // default: 'lsag-v1'
): LsagSignature
```

Produces an LSAG ring signature. Extends SAG with a deterministic key image that enables double-action detection within the same `electionId`, without cross-context linkability.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `message` | `string` | Message to sign. Any UTF-8 string, at most 65536 bytes. |
| `ring` | `string[]` | Array of x-only public key hex strings. Minimum 2, maximum 1000, no duplicates. |
| `signerIndex` | `number` | Integer index of the actual signer. Must satisfy `0 <= signerIndex < ring.length`. |
| `privateKey` | `string` | Signer's private key: 64 lowercase hex characters below the curve order. Must match `ring[signerIndex]`. |
| `electionId` | `string` | Non-empty string, at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, binding the key image to a specific context (election, vote round, rate-limit window, etc.). |
| `domain` | `string` | Optional 6th argument, after `electionId`: domain separator. Defaults to `'lsag-v1'`. Verifiers read it from the signature; see Domain Separators. |

**Returns** an `LsagSignature` object. Fully serialisable to JSON.

**Throws**
- `ValidationError`: ring too small/large, duplicate members, index out of range or not an integer, private key not 64 lowercase hex or not below the curve order, key mismatch, empty or non-string electionId, electionId over 512 bytes, message over 65536 bytes.
- A ring entry that is not a valid x-only curve point surfaces the underlying `@noble/curves` error, and a non-string ring entry a `TypeError`.

**Example**

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { lsagSign } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.publicKey);
const electionId = 'election-2026-q1';

// Sign as ring member at index 0
const sig = lsagSign('candidate-A', ring, 0, keyPairs[0].privateKey, electionId);

console.log(sig.keyImage); // deterministic 33-byte compressed point
```

---

### `lsagVerify`

```typescript
function lsagVerify(sig: LsagSignature): boolean
```

Verifies an LSAG ring signature. Returns `true` if valid, `false` otherwise. Never throws: a `null` or otherwise malformed `sig` returns `false`.

A vote verifier holds no private keys. It verifies `sig` and then uses `sig.keyImage` (not `computeKeyImage`, which needs the private key) to detect duplicates.

The domain is taken from `sig.domain`, or `'lsag-v1'` when that field is absent. There is no expected-domain parameter, and no parameter for the expected ring or `electionId`: compare those to your own values before accepting (see Verifier Checklist).

Also validates:
- `keyImage` is a valid compressed secp256k1 point (02/03 prefix, 33 bytes)
- `keyImage` is not the identity/zero point
- `electionId` is a non-empty string of at most 512 bytes

**Example**

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { lsagSign, lsagVerify } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.publicKey);
const sig = lsagSign('candidate-A', ring, 0, keyPairs[0].privateKey, 'election-2026-q1');

const valid = lsagVerify(sig);
console.log(valid); // true
```

---

### `computeKeyImage`

```typescript
function computeKeyImage(
  privateKey: string,
  publicKey: string,
  electionId: string,
): string
```

Computes `I = x * H_p(P || electionId)` — the deterministic key image for a signer in a given election.

Signer-side only: it needs the private key. The result equals `sig.keyImage` for any LSAG signature by that key in that election, so call it to check in advance whether a signer has already participated. A verifier without private keys reads `sig.keyImage` instead.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `privateKey` | `string` | Signer's private key: 64 lowercase hex characters below the curve order. |
| `publicKey` | `string` | Signer's x-only public key hex (must match `privateKey`). |
| `electionId` | `string` | Non-empty string identifying the election or context. |

**Returns** the key image as a compressed point hex string (66 hex chars).

**Throws** `ValidationError` if the private key is malformed or does not match the public key, or if `electionId` is empty or not a string.

**Example**

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { computeKeyImage } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
const privateKey = bytesToHex(secretKey);
const publicKey = bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey));

const image = computeKeyImage(privateKey, publicKey, 'election-2026-q1');
// image is a 66-character hex string beginning with '02' or '03'
```

---

### `hasDuplicateKeyImage`

```typescript
function hasDuplicateKeyImage(
  keyImage: string,
  existingImages: string[],
): boolean
```

Constant-time check — returns `true` if `keyImage` appears in `existingImages`. Using constant-time comparison prevents timing side-channel attacks.

Use this after verifying a signature to determine whether the signer has already participated in the election.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `keyImage` | `string` | Compressed point hex to search for. Must be a valid 02/03-prefixed 33-byte hex. |
| `existingImages` | `string[]` | Array of previously seen key images (e.g. from a database of accepted votes). |

**Returns** `boolean`.

**Throws** `ValidationError` if `keyImage` is not in the expected compressed-point format. A non-hex entry in `existingImages` throws a `RangeError` from the underlying hex decoder, so store only values taken from `sig.keyImage`. Entries of a different length simply do not match.

**Example**

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { lsagSign, lsagVerify, hasDuplicateKeyImage } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.publicKey);
const sig = lsagSign('candidate-A', ring, 0, keyPairs[0].privateKey, 'election-2026-q1');
if (!lsagVerify(sig)) throw new Error('Invalid signature');

const seenImages: string[] = []; // load from your database

if (hasDuplicateKeyImage(sig.keyImage, seenImages)) {
  throw new Error('Duplicate vote detected');
}

// Accept the vote and record the key image
seenImages.push(sig.keyImage);
```

---

## Error Classes

### `RingSignatureError`

```typescript
class RingSignatureError extends Error {
  name: 'RingSignatureError';
  constructor(message: string);
}
```

Base class for all errors thrown by this library.

### `ValidationError`

```typescript
class ValidationError extends RingSignatureError {
  name: 'ValidationError';
  constructor(message: string);
}
```

Thrown by `ringSign`, `lsagSign`, `computeKeyImage` and `hasDuplicateKeyImage` for invalid inputs (the verify functions never throw; they return `false`):
- Ring has fewer than 2 members
- Ring exceeds 1000 members
- Ring contains duplicate public keys
- `signerIndex` is out of bounds or not an integer
- Private key does not match the claimed ring member
- `electionId` is empty or not a string, or exceeds 512 bytes
- Key image is not a valid compressed-point hex
- `message` exceeds 65536 bytes
- A private key is non-canonical (not a valid 64-character lowercase hex value less than the curve order N)

A ring entry that is not a valid x-only curve point surfaces the underlying `@noble/curves` error, and a non-string ring entry a `TypeError`; neither is wrapped in `ValidationError`.

### `CryptoError`

```typescript
class CryptoError extends RingSignatureError {
  name: 'CryptoError';
  constructor(message: string);
}
```

Thrown for internal cryptographic failure: hash-to-point exhaustion (no valid curve point found after 256 attempts). Not expected in practice; malformed private keys and scalars raise `ValidationError`.

---

## Constants

### `MAX_RING_SIZE`

```typescript
const MAX_RING_SIZE: number = 1000;
```

Exported from the top-level entry point (re-exported from the SAG module; the LSAG module defines an identical constant that the entry point does not re-export). Maximum permitted ring members, a DoS guard against unbounded O(n) computation.

The related limits `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` (65536) and `MAX_ELECTION_ID_BYTES` (512) are internal to the source modules and are not exported.

---

## Domain Separators

Both `ringSign` and `lsagSign` include a `domain` parameter (defaults to `'sag-v1'` and `'lsag-v1'` respectively). For `ringSign` it is the 5th argument; for `lsagSign` it is the 6th, after `electionId`. The domain string is included in every hash step of the challenge chain, so editing `domain` on an existing signature makes it fail verification.

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { ringSign, ringVerify, lsagSign, lsagVerify } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    privateKey: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    publicKey: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.publicKey);
const message = 'my message';
const electionId = 'election-2026-q1';

// Namespace signatures per application
const sagSig = ringSign(message, ring, 0, keyPairs[0].privateKey, 'my-app-v1');
const lsagSig = lsagSign(message, ring, 0, keyPairs[0].privateKey, electionId, 'my-app-v1');

// The verify functions take only the signature and read the domain from it, so pin it yourself
const sagOk = sagSig.domain === 'my-app-v1' && ringVerify(sagSig); // true
const lsagOk = lsagSig.domain === 'my-app-v1' && lsagVerify(lsagSig); // true
```

### What the verifier does with the domain

`ringVerify` and `lsagVerify` take only the signature. They use `sig.domain` when present and otherwise the scheme default (`'sag-v1'` / `'lsag-v1'`). There is no expected-domain parameter. A signature made by anyone under any domain therefore verifies as it stands, so cross-protocol isolation depends on the verifier pinning the domain itself. For a custom domain, require the field to be present and equal (`sig.domain === 'my-app-v1'`, as above). For the default domain, the field is absent when signing with the default and an explicit default is equivalent, so normalise before comparing:

```typescript
import { type LsagSignature, lsagVerify } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

function verifyWithDefaultDomain(sig: LsagSignature): boolean {
  return (sig.domain ?? 'lsag-v1') === 'lsag-v1' && lsagVerify(sig);
}
```

Changing the domain breaks all existing signatures, so treat it as a protocol constant once deployed.

## Verifier Checklist

Verification proves a signature is internally consistent. It does not know what you expected. Before accepting a signature:

1. Compare `sig.ring` with the member set you expect (an attacker can sign validly over a ring of their own keys). The ring is lowercase hex, in signing order.
2. Compare `sig.message` with the message you expect.
3. LSAG: compare `sig.electionId` with the election you expect. A different `electionId` produces a different key image, which would defeat double-vote detection.
4. Pin the domain as shown above.
5. Call `ringVerify(sig)` or `lsagVerify(sig)`.
6. LSAG: call `hasDuplicateKeyImage(sig.keyImage, seenImages)`, then record `sig.keyImage`. A verifier has no private keys, so it never calls `computeKeyImage`.

## Version History and Migration

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/ring-sig/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Coming from v2 to v3, scalar hex is validated strictly: private keys, `c0` and `responses` must be exactly 64 lowercase hex characters below the curve order (3.0.0 rejects values at or above N instead of reducing them; 3.0.3 also requires the canonical 64-character lowercase form, and caps `message` at 65536 bytes and `electionId` at 512 bytes). Signatures produced by this library always satisfy these rules; hand-encoded or re-encoded scalars do not.

---

## Cryptographic Design

### SAG Construction

Schnorr-based ring signature — a cyclic challenge chain:

1. Signer picks random nonce `k`, computes `kG`.
2. Computes `c_{pi+1} = H(domain, msg, ring, kG)`.
3. For each non-signer ring member `i`: picks random `s_i`, computes `R_i = s_i*G + c_i*P_i`, then `c_{i+1} = H(domain, msg, ring, R_i)`.
4. Closes the ring: `s_pi = k - c_pi * x (mod N)`.

Verification recomputes the chain and checks that it closes: `c_n == c_0`.

Signature size is O(n): one challenge scalar plus one response scalar per ring member.

### LSAG Construction

Extends SAG with a second point chain through `H_p(P_i || electionId)`:

- Key image: `I = x * H_p(P_s || electionId)` (computed once, included in signature)
- Each step computes both `L_i = s_i*G + c_i*P_i` and `R_i = s_i*H_p(P_i || electionId) + c_i*I`
- Challenge: `c_{i+1} = H(domain, msg, ring, L_i, R_i)`

The key image is deterministic: same private key + same electionId → identical image. Different electionIds → different, unlinkable images.

### Hash-to-Point

`H_p(data)` uses SHA-256 in a try-and-increment loop to derive a curve point from arbitrary bytes. The domain separator `'secp256k1-hash-to-point-v1'` is included to prevent cross-context collisions.

### Length-Prefixed Hashing

`hashToScalar` length-prefixes every input field before concatenation. This prevents domain-separation ambiguity when fields of variable length are concatenated.

### Constant-Time Comparisons

`hasDuplicateKeyImage` and internal challenge verification use constant-time byte comparison to prevent timing side-channel attacks. Never replace with `===` or `Buffer.equals`.

**Known limitation** (see SECURITY.md, "Not constant-time"): the closing response `challenges[pi] * x` in `ringSign`/`lsagSign` uses native BigInt multiplication, which is variable-time. This is the one operation touching the secret that is not constant-time; a constant-time fix would need a scalar backend JS BigInt cannot provide, so it is an accepted, documented limitation.

---

## Complete Usage Examples

### Anonymous Group Membership Proof (SAG)

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { ringSign, ringVerify } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

// Generate keys for a group of five
const secretKeys = Array.from({ length: 5 }, () => schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey());
const privKeys = secretKeys.map(sk => bytesToHex(sk));
const pubKeys = secretKeys.map(sk => bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(sk))); // x-only

// Member at index 3 proves membership without revealing which one
const sig = ringSign(
  'I witnessed the incident at 14:32 UTC',
  pubKeys,
  3,
  privKeys[3],
);

// Any verifier can confirm a group member signed it
console.log(ringVerify(sig)); // true
console.log(sig.ring.length); // 5 — verifier knows the group, not the signer
```

### Anonymous Voting With Double-Vote Detection (LSAG)

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import {
  lsagSign,
  lsagVerify,
  hasDuplicateKeyImage,
  type LsagSignature,
} from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

// Eligible voters
const voters = Array.from({ length: 10 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    priv: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    pub: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});

const ring = voters.map(v => v.pub);
const electionId = 'community-vote-2026-q2';
const acceptedKeyImages: string[] = [];

// Verifier side: needs only the signature, no private keys
function acceptBallot(ballot: LsagSignature): 'accepted' | 'rejected' {
  if (ballot.electionId !== electionId) return 'rejected';
  if (ballot.ring.join() !== ring.join()) return 'rejected';
  if (!lsagVerify(ballot)) return 'rejected';
  if (hasDuplicateKeyImage(ballot.keyImage, acceptedKeyImages)) return 'rejected';
  acceptedKeyImages.push(ballot.keyImage);
  return 'accepted';
}

// Voter 4 casts a vote
const vote = lsagSign('option-B', ring, 4, voters[4].priv, electionId);
console.log(acceptBallot(vote)); // 'accepted'

// Voter 4 tries to vote again: same key image, detected
const secondVote = lsagSign('option-A', ring, 4, voters[4].priv, electionId);
console.log(acceptBallot(secondVote)); // 'rejected'
```

### Pre-Computing Key Images (signer side)

`computeKeyImage` needs the private key, so only the key holder (or an authority that holds the keys) can use it. It returns the same value that would appear as `sig.keyImage`.

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { computeKeyImage, hasDuplicateKeyImage } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
const priv = bytesToHex(secretKey);
const pub = bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)); // x-only
const electionId = 'community-vote-2026-q2';
const acceptedKeyImages: string[] = []; // key images already recorded by the ballot box

// Compute before signing — useful to check eligibility first
const image = computeKeyImage(priv, pub, electionId);

// Check if this voter has already participated
if (hasDuplicateKeyImage(image, acceptedKeyImages)) {
  console.log('Voter has already participated in this election.');
}
```

### Custom Domain Separation

```typescript
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js';
import { bytesToHex } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
import { ringSign, ringVerify, lsagSign, lsagVerify } from '@forgesworn/ring-sig';

const keyPairs = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => {
  const secretKey = schnorr.utils.randomSecretKey();
  return {
    priv: bytesToHex(secretKey),
    pub: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey)), // x-only
  };
});
const ring = keyPairs.map(k => k.pub);
const message = 'my message';
const index = 0;
const electionId = 'election-2026-q1';

// Namespace signatures per application; isolation needs the verifier to pin the domain
const sagSig = ringSign(message, ring, index, keyPairs[index].priv, 'my-app-sag-v1');
const lsagSig = lsagSign(message, ring, index, keyPairs[index].priv, electionId, 'my-app-lsag-v1');

const sagOk = sagSig.domain === 'my-app-sag-v1' && ringVerify(sagSig); // true
const lsagOk = lsagSig.domain === 'my-app-lsag-v1' && lsagVerify(lsagSig); // true
```

---

## When to Use Each Variant

| Requirement | Recommendation |
|-------------|---------------|
| Prove group membership — one-off, no linkability needed | SAG |
| Anonymous attestation or whistleblowing | SAG |
| Anonymous voting (one vote per person) | LSAG |
| Rate-limiting anonymous actions per time window | LSAG |
| Double-spend prevention in anonymous payment schemes | LSAG |
| Constant-size signatures regardless of ring size | Neither — use a ZK-SNARK scheme |
| Post-quantum resistance | Neither — secp256k1 is not post-quantum |

## Dependencies

Two runtime dependencies, both from the audited `@noble` family:

- `@noble/curves` — secp256k1 point operations, private key generation
- `@noble/hashes` — SHA-256, byte utilities

No other runtime dependencies.
